research_task.title: Bridge the schedule obstruction to the localized PDE residual

summary: For one explicit time-localized compact shear jet, the selected order-s residual derivative yields exactly the scale-uniform direct-injection recurrence bound. For a second explicit plateau jet with positive viscosity, the residual has two more inverse transverse-scale powers than the selected correction derivative, giving incompatible geometric thresholds for correction growth and a uniform matching-order residual. This is a bounded statement about the specified localized model, not a Navier--Stokes breakdown result.

value_assessment.novelty: The supplied prior artifacts separately gave a static forced-Euler localization residual and an abstract schedule obstruction. This attempt adds the missing interval cutoff, derives the abstract direct-injection factor from the localized PDE residual, and identifies the two-derivative viscosity gap absent from the Euler calculation.
value_assessment.evidence: A componentwise derivation records the exact cutoff residual, coordinate Jacobian, all fixed-order anisotropic scale monomials, and two cancellation-free compact local-jet evaluations. The exponent incompatibility follows by exact algebra; the prepared enumeration was not executed and is not counted as evidence.
value_assessment.falsifier: A componentwise recalculation producing a nonzero competing first-component term on either stated local jet, or a valid scale choice with positive beta satisfying both gamma below beta s and gamma at least beta times s plus two, would overturn the corresponding scoped claim.

claims.statement: For one interval, fixed integer s at least zero, and the stated degree-s compact shear core, a scale-uniform W^{s,infinity} residual bound implies that the outgoing selected derivative amplitude is at most exp of the integrated absolute affine strain times C_s d.
claims.evidence_summary: Exact evaluation makes cutoff switching the only nonzero contribution to the selected residual derivative, and the fundamental theorem of calculus supplies the inverse interval length.
claims.verification_method: Recompute the cutoff residual component, differentiate s times in the transverse direction, evaluate the local polynomial jet, and apply the fundamental theorem of calculus.

claims.statement: For the stated compact plateau shear core with positive viscosity, the order-s residual contains two additional inverse transverse-scale powers; under a geometric schedule, correction growth requires gamma below beta s while uniform matching-order residual control requires gamma at least beta times s plus two.
claims.evidence_summary: At the core the affine and quadratic first-component terms vanish, while exact differentiation of the Laplacian gives minus nu A S times Ly to the negative s plus two power.
claims.verification_method: Differentiate the displayed local polynomial jet directly and subtract the two geometric scale exponents.

limitations: The pointwise lower bounds apply to explicit profile jets and the residual representative using the fixed affine pressure, not to every profile or arbitrary pressure redistribution.
Cancellation after Leray projection or among multiple simultaneous corrections is not analyzed.
The viscous obstruction requires positive viscosity and disappears in the forced-Euler case.
The prepared exact-integer enumeration was not executed and supplies no computational evidence.
No accumulating construction, smooth global forcing scheme, or finite-time breakdown is established.
failed_approaches: A termwise divergent upper bound alone would not prove failure of uniform residual control because terms could cancel; explicit local polynomial jets were used instead to isolate the switching and viscous terms.
The exact-integer exponent audit was prepared but could not be executed before finalization, so the result relies on the displayed analytic subtraction only.
next_actions: Test the viscous scale gap with a compact divergence-free dual projection that is invariant under pressure redistribution.
Audit whether several overlapping corrections can cancel the isolated projected term while preserving the intended amplification schedule.
Execute the prepared exact-arithmetic exponent audit as independent reproducibility evidence.

proposed_tasks.title: Project the viscous gap through Leray
proposed_tasks.objective: Replace the fixed-pressure pointwise lower bound by a pressure-invariant divergence-free dual estimate for one compact correction.
proposed_tasks.rationale: Pressure redistribution and multi-correction cancellation are the principal unresolved limitations of the current two-derivative gap.
proposed_tasks.success_criteria: Produce a scale-explicit divergence-free projection lower bound retaining two additional inverse transverse-scale powers.
proposed_tasks.useful_failure_criteria: Exhibit an exact pressure or nonlinear cancellation that removes the proposed projected lower bound.
proposed_tasks.verification_method: Construct an explicit compact divergence-free test field, integrate by parts exactly, and audit every profile constant and anisotropic scale.

proposed_tasks.title: Reproduce the cutoff exponent audit
proposed_tasks.objective: Independently verify the switching recurrence and geometric viscosity mismatch with exact arithmetic and boundary cases.
proposed_tasks.rationale: The present bounded result is analytic only because the prepared exact-integer audit was not executed.
proposed_tasks.success_criteria: Confirm the residual identity and two-beta gap for representative and bounded families of integer exponents, with positive controls.
proposed_tasks.useful_failure_criteria: Identify a sign, derivative-order, or scale-substitution error and state the corrected threshold.
proposed_tasks.verification_method: Use an independent component derivation and exact integer or rational arithmetic; distinguish bounded enumeration from proof.
